summary: The 13 dimension auditors covered their lanes well but collectively missed whole CATEGORIES: (A) non-functional/performance acceptance criteria (PRD §19.6's 7 named latency metrics) have ZERO owner anywhere; (B) the native desktop notification subsystem (DESK-8) is referenced only as an unowned outbox 'notifier' destination — no module, no flow, no event, no macOS permission-consent step; (C) accessibility (PRD §14.8 MUST: drag non-drag alternatives, graph list/table fallbacks) is in 0 dimension files; (D) three PRD §10 MVP surfaces — Usage/Context/Cost Dashboard (§10.18, an MVP must-have the draft's own §11 screen list OMITS), Settings integration-health (SET-3 MUST), and external-IDE open (EDIT-10) — appear in no finding; (E) the biggest second-order problem: the dimensions independently demand 'pick ONE canonical X' for the SAME shared objects (actor enum, Session states, Task/PlanTask, ID format, ActorRef) with DIFFERENT proposed resolutions and ALL needs_human — an un-converged decision CLUSTER of ~25-30 load-bearing human decisions that no one sequenced or reconciled, and which D13's mandatory Appendix A cannot be written until they resolve; (F) cross-artifact contradiction not assembled by any single auditor: Brain is 'never hard-depended on' (§13/§15) yet demo steps 11-16 are MANDATORY Brain beats AND D06's 2026-06-15 Agent-SDK credit-pool can HALT the demo mid-run — three artifacts disagree about whether the demo can even run; (G) buildability: nobody assessed whether the post-fix doc (draft + ~70 fixes + Appendix A + new sub-anchors) is finalize-able and the slice buildable by a solo+AI team, which is the prompt's 'can it actually be built' test.

findings.finding: NON-FUNCTIONAL / PERFORMANCE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA HAVE NO OWNER ACROSS ALL 13 DIMENSIONS. PRD §19.6 names seven performance success metrics — App launch time, Project scan time, Terminal attach latency, Graph render time, Diff open latency, Event write latency, Project Brain drawer response latency — as binding success criteria. The architecture draft sets NO budget for any of them; the word 'performance' appears in 0 dimension findings and 'latency' only in D09 (and there only for the SQLite single-writer load test, NOT the 7 PRD metrics). These are exactly the cross-cutting NFRs that fall between dimensions: D02-states owns enums, D03 owns failures, D09 owns test mechanism — but no one owns the latency-budget targets the tests must assert against. This is a second-order consequence of the locked architecture too: the projection-driven UDS-IPC + serialized-single-writer design (ADR-003/004) has inherent latency on the read path (UI -> UDS -> projection query) and the write path (intent -> UDS -> serialized write-actor -> event+projection+outbox txn) that DIRECTLY governs 'Event write latency' and 'drawer response latency' — yet no budget bounds it, so the architecture's central performance bet is unfalsifiable.
findings.evidence: PRD §19.6 (lines 2263-2273) lists the 7 metrics as Success Metrics. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT has no latency/budget section (grep 'performance'/'latency'/'p95'/'budget' returns only the git2 'hot reads' phrase and the §18.2 'usage budgets' deferral — neither is a perf NFR). D09 finding 7 flags the SQLite load test has no pass/fail number but scopes it to write-contention only, not the 7 UI-facing metrics. The §11 frontend section and §14 testing section name no rendering/attach/diff-open budget.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md a §Non-Functional Requirements / Performance Budgets section (or fold into §14 Testing + §11 Frontend) that assigns a committed target to each PRD §19.6 metric (e.g. app launch <Xs, terminal attach <Xms, diff open <Xms, event-write p95 <Xms, drawer response <Xs), name the owning module for each, and make each a falsifiable assertion in the §14 test taxonomy (extending D09's tiering). Tie event-write-latency and drawer-latency budgets to the ADR-003/004 single-writer + UDS design so the architecture's core performance bet is bounded and testable.

findings.finding: UNRECONCILED CROSS-DIMENSION DECISION CLUSTER: five dimensions independently demand 'pick ONE canonical' for the SAME shared objects with DIFFERENT proposed resolutions and ALL marked needs_human — but no one sequences or reconciles them, and D13's MANDATORY Appendix A (model inventory) literally cannot be authored until they resolve. The actor/requester enum is flagged by BOTH D07 (critical: EM §7 vs AG §9.7 vs DATA_MODEL three-way, recommend EM tokens canonical) AND D13 (ActorRef sub-anchor) AND D05/D02 (remote_device vs remote_client) — three findings, no single owner. Session states are flagged by D02 (add changes_ready -> 17 states) AND D12 (the '16 vs 17' count blocks the D3 diagram) AND D13 (§5.1 enum anchor) — and the count the diagram must use is undecided. Task-vs-PlanTask is flagged by D02 (nice-to-have), D05 (critical SoT), D07 (important, needs ADR-012) — three different severities for ONE decision. ID format (ULID vs UUIDv7) is D07-important AND D09 (determinism). The net effect no single auditor sees: ~25-30 needs_human decisions, many MUTUALLY DEPENDENT (the actor-enum choice changes ActorRef which changes the event envelope which changes Appendix A which changes every projection), arriving at finalize as an unordered pile. Finalize will thrash unless they are resolved as ONE reconciliation pass in dependency order.
findings.evidence: Cross-reading: D07 finding 1 (actor enum, critical, needs_human) + D13 finding 5/6 (ActorRef + envelope anchors, needs_human) + D05 finding on Codex map + D02 finding on remote_client. D02 finding 1 (changes_ready) + D12 finding 6 (16-vs-17 count blocks D3) + D13 finding 2 (§5.1 enum anchor). Task/PlanTask: D02 finding 13 (nice-to-have), D05 finding 2 (critical), D07 finding 2 (important) — same decision, 3 severities. D13 finding 1 says Appendix A is mandatory and must list these exact enums/IDs — so it cannot be written until the enums/IDs are locked. Counting needs_human across D01-D13: ~28 are true.
findings.proposed_fix: Before writing ARCHITECTURE.md, run a SINGLE 'shared-contract reconciliation' pass (new pre-finalize step) that resolves the interdependent decisions in dependency order: (1) ID format -> (2) actor/requester enum + ActorRef -> (3) event envelope (depends on actor enum) -> (4) the 8+ state-machine enums incl. changes_ready and Session count -> (5) Task-vs-PlanTask table shape -> then (6) author D13's Appendix A from the locked set. Add a §0 'Decision Ledger' to ARCHITECTURE.md recording each resolution once, so the ~28 needs_human items are decided as a connected graph, not piecemeal. Flag to the human that these are a coupled set, not independent toggles.

findings.finding: CROSS-ARTIFACT CONTRADICTION ON WHETHER THE DEMO CAN EVEN RUN — assembled from three artifacts no single dimension auditor combined. (1) The architecture asserts Brain is OPTIONAL and 'the platform never hard-depends on Brain' / 'degrades gracefully when absent/stale' (§13, §15, Law #3). (2) But PRD §25 demo steps 11-16 (Brain drawer read -> ask Brain why-feature -> evidence chips -> ask Brain to create PR -> Brain proposes action plan -> approve) are MANDATORY demo beats, and §18.1 step 11 makes Brain-propose-PR-plan MVP-blocking. (3) D06 (deps) found the 2026-06-15 Agent-SDK separate credit pool can HARD-STOP all SDK-driven Claude supervision (no fallback) — which means the demo's own Claude session (step 6, and every supervised action) can die mid-demo on a cost-exhausted account. D10 partially touched the sidecar-fallback-vs-demo conflict, but no one assembled the full three-way contradiction: the architecture says Brain-optional, the demo says Brain-mandatory, and the dep research says the Claude path underpinning the whole demo can silently halt. These cannot all be true. Either the demo is NOT runnable as a credibility proof under the locked constraints, or 'Brain optional' is false for MVP, or the credit-pool risk invalidates the SDK-primary decision for the demo.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §13 ('platform never hard-depends on Brain'; 'degrades gracefully when absent/stale'), §15 (Brain has zero privileged ops), §4.2 Law #3. PRD §25 steps 11-16 (Brain-driven) + §18.1 step 11 ('[LOCKED]' MVP slice requires Brain propose a PR action plan). D06-deps finding 2 (Agent-SDK credit pool, no auto-fallback, 'automated requests stop entirely', demo not verified to avoid pool draw). D10-deploy finding 3 (Brain-optional vs demo-requires-Brain noted ONLY for the sidecar notarization fallback, not the full contradiction). D08-scope finding 2 separately argues Brain-propose-PR is P1-pulled-into-MVP.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve in ARCHITECTURE.md §1/§13/§18.1 with one explicit statement: the §25 demo path REQUIRES a reachable Brain (via primary sidecar OR a chosen fallback) and a non-exhausted Claude execution profile — these are demo PREconditions, while NON-demo features degrade gracefully when Brain is absent. Add a demo-precondition checklist (Brain reachable; Claude profile has SDK-pool budget OR demo uses interactive-PTY path that doesn't draw the pool). Reconcile with D06 finding 2 (decide SDK-driven vs interactive-PTY default for the demo) and D08 finding 2 (whether step 14-16 must be Brain-driven or a direct UI Create-PR satisfies the demo). This is a load-bearing human decision about demo viability under the locked constraints.

findings.finding: NATIVE DESKTOP NOTIFICATION SUBSYSTEM (DESK-8) IS AN UNOWNED MODULE — referenced only as an outbox-drainer destination ('the notifier', §10) with no module in §6, no flow in §8, no event taxonomy, no macOS permission-consent step, and no presence in the §11 screen/feature list. PRD DESK-8 (SHOULD) and the MVP nice-to-have 'Native desktop notifications' require local notifications for waiting sessions, failed checks, permission requests, and completed sessions — and the entire product thesis ('human attention is the scarce resource', PRD §5.2) depends on PUSHING attention events to the user, not just rendering them in-app. No dimension owns this: D01-flows mapped the Human Input Queue resolution flow but not the notification EMISSION; D04-interfaces enumerated the brain MCP-notification adapter (a different 'notification'); D11-security never considered the macOS notification-permission grant as a consent/trust event. Second-order: macOS requires a user permission grant for notifications, which is itself a first-run setup-wizard consent step (DESK-8 + §9.1 'consented setup') that D01's setup-flow gap did not enumerate, and a notification carrying session/task context is a potential information-leak surface (lock-screen previews) D11 did not assess.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §10 'Outbox drainers — deliver to Brain (MCP), GitHub/Linear syncers, the notifier' — the ONLY mention; no `notifier`/`notifications` module in §6 table, no row in §8 flows, no entry in §11 MVP feature list. PRD DESK-8 (line 516-518), PRD §15 MVP nice-to-have 'Native desktop notifications' (line 2111), PRD §5.2 attention-first thesis. 'notif' in dimension findings (D04/D05/D09/D11/D13) refers exclusively to Brain MCP notifications, never the desktop notifier.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md a `notifier` module to §6 (consumes specific event types via the outbox: SessionWaitingOnHuman/Permission, CheckFailed, SessionCompleted -> macOS UserNotification), a §8 flow row ('Emit attention notification'), the macOS notification-permission grant as a §9.1/setup-wizard consent step, and a §15 note on notification-content redaction (no secrets/sensitive context in lock-screen previews). Tag desktop notifications MVP-nice-to-have per PRD §15. Cross-link DESK-8 and the attention thesis (§5.2).

findings.finding: ACCESSIBILITY (PRD §14.8, a MUST) IS UNCOVERED BY ALL 13 DIMENSIONS. PRD §14.8 states 'Drag-and-drop must have non-drag alternatives. Graph views must have list/table alternatives' — both MUST requirements, reinforced by TASK-5 (every drag action MUST have an accessible button/menu alternative) and OBS-6 (graph MUST have list/table alternatives). 'accessib'/'a11y' appear in 0 dimension findings. The draft mentions list/table fallback once in passing (§11, citing UX §5.7) but assigns no owner, no acceptance criterion, and no test. D09-testing built a frontend test tier but it covers attention-ordering and approval-card rendering — NOT a11y conformance (keyboard navigation, non-drag alternatives, screen-reader labels, the list-fallback equivalence to the graph). This is a classic cross-cutting concern that falls between D01 (flows), D09 (testing), and the UX spec: a MUST requirement with no home in the binding architecture.
findings.evidence: PRD §14.8 (line 2060), TASK-5 (line 1112 'every drag action MUST have an accessible button/menu alternative'), OBS-6 (line 1617 'The graph MUST have list/table alternatives'). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §11 mentions 'Graph surfaces always have list/table fallbacks (UX §5.7)' once, with no test or owner. grep accessib/a11y over docs/gap-audits/D01-D13 = 0 hits.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §11 (Frontend) an explicit accessibility-invariant: every drag interaction has a button/menu equivalent (TASK-5), every graph surface has a functionally-equivalent list/table (OBS-6), keyboard-navigability for the command palette and queues. Add an a11y test row to the §14 frontend test tier (D09): assert each drag action has a non-drag path and each graph view a list fallback. Make these MUSTs falsifiable rather than prose.

findings.finding: THREE PRD §10 MVP SURFACES HAVE ZERO COVERAGE IN ANY FINDING — Usage/Context/Cost Dashboard, Settings integration-health, and external-IDE open. (1) The Usage/Context/Cost Dashboard (PRD §7.17, §10.18 USAGE-1..5) is an explicit MVP MUST-HAVE ('Usage/context display with exact/estimated/unavailable labels', PRD §15 line 2097) — yet the draft's §11 MVP demo-screen list OMITS it entirely (it lists Command Center, Project Home/Graph, Sessions, Terminal, Code/Diff, Plan View, Human Input Queue, Gateway modal, Brain drawer, Execution Profiles, Events/Audit — NO Usage Dashboard). The draft HAS a `usage` daemon module (§6) producing the data, but no UI surface to display it, so an MVP must-have produces metering with nowhere to show it. USAGE-* appears in D05 (source-of-truth of the fields) and D11 (credential security) but neither audits the dashboard SURFACE. (2) SET-3 (Settings MUST show integration health and auth status) has no flow/screen/finding. (3) EDIT-10 (open in external IDE, SHOULD) has no finding. These are requirements-with-no-coverage — precisely the PRD-module-with-no-finding gap the completeness pass exists to catch.
findings.evidence: PRD §15 MVP must-have line 2097 'Usage/context display with exact/estimated/unavailable labels'; PRD §7.17 + §10.18 USAGE-1..5; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §11 MVP screen list (line 213) omits the Usage Dashboard though §6 has a `usage` module. SET-3 (line 1694, MUST) — grep 'integration health'/'SET-3' over D01-D13 = 0. EDIT-10 (line 1073) — grep 'external IDE'/'EDIT-10' over D01-D13 = 0.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md: (1) add the Usage/Context/Cost Dashboard to the §11 MVP screen list (it is a PRD §15 must-have) and a §8 flow row reading the `usage` module's projection with exact/estimated/unavailable labels (USAGE-4); (2) add a Settings integration-health surface/flow (SET-3) showing auth status per integration (octocrab/Linear/keychain self-test) — reuse D03's integration-failure states; (3) add the external-IDE-open action (EDIT-10) as a low-risk Gateway intent or direct UI action in the Code/Diff review flow. Tag each by its PRD priority.

findings.finding: BUILDABILITY / FINALIZE-ABILITY OF THE POST-FIX DOCUMENT IS UNASSESSED — the prompt's 'can the finalized doc actually be built from the draft+fixes' test. Aggregating across all 13 dimensions: the fixes add an entirely new §Failure-Mode Contract (D03), §Non-Functional/Performance section (D14), Appendix A (D13), §5.1/§5.2/§5.3 sub-anchors (D13), §6.1/§6.2 Gateway contract sub-anchors (D04/D13), §7.1 envelope anchor (D13), a 20-row MVP action-type catalog (D04), an MVP event-type registry (D04), an MCP-notification->event mapping table (D04), a HarnessAdapter trait+normalized-types spec (D04), a version-compatibility matrix (D10), first-run bootstrap + update/daemon-lifecycle + sign/notarize subsections (D10), a test taxonomy with fault-injection/clock/FakeHarness seams (D09), and ~28 needs_human decisions. That is a near-rewrite, not a finalize-edit — yet the draft §18.1 is tagged [LOCKED] and the build constraint is 'solo build driven largely by AI agents.' No dimension assessed whether (a) the resulting doc is internally consistent after all fixes land, (b) the §18.1 build ORDER survives the fixes (e.g. D08 wants Codex deferred to P1, which reorders step 7; D10 wants first-run-bootstrap before step 1's daemon-skeleton), or (c) the slice + fixes is achievable for the stated team. The risk: finalize produces a doc that is complete but un-sequenced and larger than the build capacity, defeating the 'credible demoable MVP' goal.
findings.evidence: Aggregate of D03 (new failure section), D04 (5 new contract tables), D09 (test seams), D10 (4 new deploy subsections), D13 (Appendix A + ~6 sub-anchors), D14 (perf section, notifier, a11y, 3 surfaces). D08-scope finding 5 notes the §18.1 '[LOCKED]' tag conflicts with the handoff calling the slice 'still being pressure-tested' but does not assess cumulative buildability. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT preamble line 5 ('solo build driven largely by AI agents'; 'credible demoable MVP over a calendar deadline'). No dimension contains 'cumulative'/'build order soundness'/'finalize-able'.
findings.proposed_fix: Before/within finalize: (1) re-derive the §18.1 build order AFTER applying the scope cuts (D08) and the bootstrap/deploy ordering (D10) — first-run bootstrap + version-compat must precede the daemon skeleton; the Codex deferral reorders the harness steps. (2) Add a one-page 'finalize delta' note listing which sections are NEW vs EDITED so the human sees this is a major revision, not a touch-up, and re-tag §18.1 from [LOCKED] to reflect the post-audit decision. (3) State a buildability check: the Tier-0 demo-critical executor set (D08) + the spine, with everything else explicitly P1, so the slice is sized to the solo+AI build capacity.

findings.finding: SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE OF LOCKED DECISIONS: THE OS-PERMISSION / TCC CONSENT SURFACE IS UNMAPPED ACROSS THE WHOLE STACK. The locked decisions (detached daemon owning PTYs + git + FS + keychain; bundled Python sidecar; native runtime) each trigger a macOS permission/TCC prompt that no dimension assembled into a single consent map: (a) keychain ACL prompts (D10 touched signing-stability but not the consent UX), (b) macOS notification permission (D14 finding 4), (c) Full Disk Access / file-access prompts when the daemon reads arbitrary local repos under ~/ and ~/Library, (d) the launchd-registered detached daemon being a Login Item / Background Item the user must approve (macOS 13+ Background Items management via SMAppService), (e) AppleEvents/automation prompts if 'open in external IDE' (EDIT-10) scripts another app. PRD §9.1 mandates 'consented' setup and §14.7 mandates visible degraded states — but the union of OS consent gates the locked architecture provokes is owned by nobody. D11-security audited the trust boundaries and redaction; D10 audited signing; D01 audited the setup flow — but the macOS-consent surface specifically (a direct second-order effect of detached-daemon + native-runtime) is between all three.
findings.evidence: Locked: detached daemon via launchd (ADR-002), keychain (ADR-007/011), bundled sidecar (ADR-005). PRD §9.1 'setup must be consented' (line 539); PRD §14.7 degraded states. macOS 13+ requires user approval for launchd Background Items (SMAppService); Full Disk Access is required to read many ~/Library paths (incl. ~/.codex, ~/.claude transcripts the adapters tail). No dimension finding contains 'TCC'/'Full Disk Access'/'Background Item'/'Login Item'/'notification permission' as a consent surface.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md a §First-Run Consent / OS-Permission map (in §16 bootstrap or §9.1 setup): enumerate each macOS consent gate the locked architecture triggers — keychain ACL (post-signing), notification permission, file-access/Full-Disk-Access for reading repos + ~/.claude/~/.codex transcripts, launchd Background Item approval (SMAppService), AppleEvents for external-IDE — with the setup-wizard step and degraded-state for each denial (PRD §14.7). Cross-link D10 (signing/bootstrap), D11 (trust boundaries), D01 (setup flow).

findings.finding: NO ARTIFACT OWNS THE iOS-COMPANION SEAM VERIFICATION even though it is the stated justification for two locked/early decisions. The architecture repeatedly cites 'iOS-ready' as rationale: the GatewayPort/UDS seam exists 'from day one (which the future iOS companion reuses)' (§4.3), the GatewayPort trait is 'framework-decoupled and iOS-ready' (§6), RemoteClient is a gap object (DATA_MODEL §6), and AG-8/§18.3 require remote actions to route through the Gateway. Yet no dimension verified that the seam as designed actually supports the iOS capabilities PRD §18.1 names (observability, push for human-input, low-risk approvals, single-session short-instruction) — e.g. the UDS transport is explicitly local-only and the future companion needs a relay/tunnel (PRD §18.3), so 'the iOS companion reuses the UDS GatewayPort' is questionable (it reuses the TRAIT, not the UDS transport). D04 enumerated the GatewayPort method gap; D13 anchored RemoteClient as dormant-scaffolding; but no one checked the load-bearing 'iOS-ready' CLAIM that justifies building the seam now. If the seam is NOT actually reusable for iOS, the cost of building the IPC seam day-one (paid in MVP complexity) is partly unjustified.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4.3 ('explicit IPC seam from day one (which the future iOS companion reuses)'), §6 ('keeps it framework-decoupled and iOS-ready'). PRD §18.3 'Remote companion requires a secure relay or tunnel model later' — i.e. NOT the local UDS. AG-8 (remote actions through Gateway), §18.1 iOS capabilities. D04 finding (GatewayPort methods undefined) and D13 finding (RemoteClient dormant) touch the pieces but not the reuse claim.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a one-paragraph note to ARCHITECTURE.md §6/§13: clarify that the iOS companion reuses the GatewayPort TRAIT + ActionRequest/intent model, NOT the UDS transport (which is local-only); the future relay/tunnel (PRD §18.3) terminates at a daemon-side adapter that re-injects intents through the same trait. State the minimal seam properties that make this true (transport-agnostic trait, RemoteClient actor already modeled, all remote actions are ActionRequests) so the 'iOS-ready' justification for the day-one IPC seam is explicit and checkable, not assumed.

findings.finding: DEMO STEP 7 ('Session appears in sidebar AND project graph') implies a real-time cross-surface propagation guarantee that no dimension specified: a single SessionStarted event must fan out to BOTH proj_session (sidebar) and proj_project_graph (graph) projections and reach the UI live. The draft has both projections (DATA_MODEL §2.3) and the projection->UI subscription (§11), but no one asserted the consistency/latency property the demo visibly depends on — that the same event updates multiple projections atomically and the UI re-renders both surfaces from one push. D02 covered the AgentTeam projection gap; D05 covered which projection is canonical; D09 covered projection rebuild-equivalence testing — but the multi-projection fan-out + live-push consistency that demo step 7 showcases (and that the 'projection-driven reattaching client' model rests on) is unspecified and untested. Related: the graph's 14 node types (OBS-2) and the sidebar's attention-ordering must agree on the same session's status in real time.
findings.evidence: PRD §25 step 7 'Session appears in sidebar and project graph'; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §11 (projection-driven client) + DATA_MODEL §2.3 (proj_session + proj_project_graph both exist). No dimension finding asserts the single-event->multi-projection fan-out consistency or its live-push to multiple surfaces; D09's projection tests assert rebuild-equivalence, not multi-projection coherence.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to ARCHITECTURE.md §7/§10 a statement that a single event may update multiple projections within the one event-commit transaction (event+projections+outbox), and that the UI subscription pushes projection deltas so all subscribed surfaces (sidebar, graph, queue) reflect the same event coherently. Add a §14 test: emit SessionStarted -> assert proj_session and proj_project_graph both reflect it after the same txn, and a UI test that both surfaces re-render from one push (extends D09's frontend tier).
